prompt.context_jp: 事件の余波___広がる本店の廊下で、花咲舞はひとり窓辺に立ちつくしていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 事件の余波___広がる本店の廊下
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks new information inside a relative clause.

feedback.correct_en: Inside a relative clause modifying 廊下, the subject typically takes が. 余波 is new descriptive information about the hallway, not a topic being commented on.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark a topic, but relative clauses rarely host topics. を would require a transitive verb; 広がる is intransitive here.

contrast_examples.en: As for rain, it doesn't fall. (topic-level statement)

prompt.context_jp: 一皿目に運ばれてきたのは、幸三ご自慢の一品であった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 一皿目に運ばれてきたの___、幸三ご自慢の一品であった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for this cleft-like 〜のは〜 structure.

feedback.correct_en: The 〜のは〜だ cleft pattern uses は to set up 'what was brought first' as the topic, with 幸三ご自慢の一品 as the predicate identification.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would turn this into exhaustive listing of a subject, breaking the cleft structure. を doesn't fit here.

prompt.context_jp: 舞___カウンターに頬を膨らませたまま、父を睨みつける。
prompt.prompt_jp: 舞___カウンターに頬を膨らませたまま、父を睨みつける。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking Mai as the ongoing topic.

feedback.correct_en: Mai is already the established protagonist; the narration continues to describe her actions, so は marks her as the topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce her as new information, which clashes with the ongoing narrative focus on Mai.

contrast_examples.en: Mai (as topic) glared at her father.
It was Mai who glared at her father. (identificational)

prompt.context_jp: そこには早くに亡くなった妻の写真___飾られ、毎朝欠かさず一輪の花を供えているのだと、舞はよく知っている。
prompt.prompt_jp: そこには早くに亡くなった妻の写真___飾られ...
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that introduces this photo as new information.

feedback.correct_en: The photo is being introduced to the reader for the first time with an existential/descriptive verb (飾られ). New-information subjects of this kind take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose the photo as a known topic, which it isn't yet in the narration.

contrast_examples.en: There is a book on the desk. (introducing it)

contrast_examples.jp: その本は机の上にある。
contrast_examples.en: That book is on the desk. (already known)

prompt.context_jp: 湯呑みを持つ幸三の手___、ほんの少しだけ止まった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 湯呑みを持つ幸三の手___、ほんの少しだけ止まった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'Kōzō's hand' as the newly-focused subject.

feedback.correct_en: The narration zooms in on a specific detail — his hand pausing. New visual information like this is marked with が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make it a general comment about his hand, losing the sudden-detail nuance.

prompt.context_jp: 舞の声___低く、しかし怒りをはらんでいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 舞の声___低く、しかし怒りをはらんでいた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the topic 'Mai's voice'.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence makes a characterizing comment ('low, yet full of anger') about Mai's voice as a topic — classic は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would read as newly-presented information or exhaustive identification, which doesn't fit this descriptive statement.

contrast_examples.en: It was the voice that was low. (identifying what was low)

prompt.context_jp: 「“手柄___上司のもの ミスは部下のもの”」
prompt.prompt_jp: 手柄___上司のもの、ミス___部下のもの
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particles that produce the parallel-contrast motto.

feedback.correct_en: Both slots take contrastive は: 'As for credit — the boss's; as for mistakes — the subordinates'.' Parallel は...は is the hallmark of this kind of maxim.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark each as new/identificational, breaking the proverb-like contrast structure that makes the saying memorable.

contrast_examples.jp: 肉は食べる、魚は食べない。
contrast_examples.en: Meat I eat; fish I don't. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 「悪いの___支店長なのに 本人は何の傷も負わないで」
prompt.prompt_jp: 悪いの___支店長なのに
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the 'the one at fault is...' cleft.

feedback.correct_en: 悪いのは〜 is a cleft/topic structure meaning 'as for who is at fault, it's the branch manager'. The のは…だ frame requires は.
feedback.incorrect_en: 悪いのが… would awkwardly identify 'the bad thing' as a new subject, missing the contrastive-topic nuance Mai intends.

contrast_examples.en: The one at fault is me.
I'm the one who's at fault. (exhaustive)

prompt.context_jp: 熱くなった舞の腕___カウンターの小鉢に触れ、乾いた音を立てた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 熱くなった舞の腕___カウンターの小鉢に触れ...
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that reports this sudden event.

feedback.correct_en: This is a sudden, event-reporting sentence ('her arm brushed the bowl'). Event-reporting subjects take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn it into a general statement about her arm, losing the on-the-spot event feel.

prompt.context_jp: 杉下という若い行員の未来___、上司の一存で押しつぶされんとしている...
prompt.prompt_jp: 杉下という若い行員の未来___、上司の一存で押しつぶされんとしていること
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle inside this subordinate clause.

feedback.correct_en: Inside a こと-nominalized clause, the subject takes が. The whole clause becomes the thing Mai 'can't accept'.
feedback.incorrect_en: は rarely appears as the plain subject marker inside such embedded こと-clauses.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が来ることを知らなかった。
contrast_examples.en: I didn't know that he was coming.

contrast_examples.jp: ×彼は来ることを知らなかった。

prompt.context_jp: 「お前が言ってることは正論だよ そんなこと___みんな分かってる」
prompt.prompt_jp: そんなこと___みんな分かってる
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 'that sort of thing' as topic.

feedback.correct_en: Souma is making a general comment: 'as for that kind of thing, everyone knows'. Fronted topic + comment = は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 'that kind of thing' a new subject being identified, which doesn't fit Souma's resigned tone.

contrast_examples.jp: そんなことはみんな知ってる。

prompt.context_jp: 「銀行___ そんな特別なんですか？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 銀行___そんな特別なんですか？
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle in Mai's accusatory topic question.

feedback.correct_en: って is a casual topic marker, equivalent to は, perfect for Mai's blunt 'is banking really that special?' challenge.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark 'banking' as new information, which clashes with Mai treating 'banking' as a repeated topic from Souma's lines.

prompt.context_jp: 「ウワサの真偽___ 本人たちにしか分からない」
prompt.prompt_jp: ウワサの真偽___ 本人たちにしか分からない
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the fronted topic 'the truth of the rumor'.

feedback.correct_en: Karashima brings up 'the truth of the rumor' as a topic to comment on: only the people involved know. Fronted known-topic → は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it an identificational subject ('IT is the truth of the rumor that…'), which is not what Karashima is saying.

contrast_examples.jp: 真相は彼しか知らない。
真相が明らかになった。

prompt.context_jp: 「当行に口座がある___いうことです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 当行に口座___ある、ということです。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'has an account at our bank'.

feedback.correct_en: The existential verb ある takes が for its subject here — this is a new fact being presented as the common point.
feedback.incorrect_en: 口座は would presuppose 'account' as a known topic; the narrative is instead introducing the shared trait.

contrast_examples.en: I have an account at the bank.

contrast_examples.jp: 口座はまだ開いていない。
contrast_examples.en: As for the account, I haven't opened one yet.

prompt.context_jp: 扉を開けたの___、青山支店を率いる新田隼夫であった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 扉を開けたの___、新田隼夫であった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for this 'the one who opened the door' cleft.

feedback.correct_en: 〜のは〜だ cleft pattern — fronting 'the one who opened the door' as topic and identifying him. は is required by this structure.
feedback.incorrect_en: が doesn't fit the 〜のは〜だ cleft; it would be ungrammatical here.

contrast_examples.en: The one who opened the shop is my father.

prompt.context_jp: 「あの___ような ものの言い方」
prompt.prompt_jp: あの___ような ものの言い方
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that fits Mai's complaint about Nitta's attitude.

feedback.correct_en: 見下す = 'to look down on / condescend'. Mai is criticizing Nitta's condescending manner of speech.
feedback.incorrect_en: 見上げる means to look up to (admiring), the opposite nuance. 見送る means to see off.

prompt.context_jp: 「お父さん？ つい ___が滑っちゃって」
prompt.prompt_jp: つい___が滑っちゃって
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the body part for 'it slipped out'.

feedback.correct_en: 口が滑る is the set idiom meaning 'to let something slip (that you shouldn't say).' Kōzō accidentally revealed Mai got dumped.
feedback.incorrect_en: 手が滑る means dropping something physically; 足が滑る means slipping with your foot. Neither matches a verbal gaffe.

contrast_examples.en: It slipped out of my mouth.

contrast_examples.jp: 手が滑って皿を落とした。
contrast_examples.en: My hand slipped and I dropped the plate.

prompt.context_jp: 「ありがとうございます ___に銘じます」
prompt.prompt_jp: ___に銘じます
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the body part in this formal expression.

feedback.correct_en: 肝に銘じる is the fixed idiom meaning 'to engrave on one's liver' = to take deeply to heart. It's standard for responding to a superior's warning.
feedback.incorrect_en: 心に or 胸に are used in other expressions (心に残る, 胸に秘める) but not with 銘じる.

contrast_examples.en: I'll keep that in mind as I work.

prompt.context_jp: 「このままだと___ぞ ウチの5000万」
prompt.prompt_jp: このままだと___ぞ、ウチの5000万
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the banking verb for a loan going bad.

feedback.correct_en: 焦げ付く literally 'to get burnt onto a pan' is the standard banking term for a loan becoming unrecoverable.
feedback.incorrect_en: 焼け付く (sun blazing) and 凍り付く (freezing over) are vivid but not banking jargon for bad debt.

prompt.context_jp: 「甘やかしては ほかの行員たちに ___がつきませんから」
prompt.prompt_jp: ほかの行員たちに___がつきません
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the noun that completes 'can't set an example'.

feedback.correct_en: 示しがつかない is a fixed phrase: 'it won't set an example / won't maintain discipline' before others.
feedback.incorrect_en: 見せ and 知らせ are real words but don't form this idiom with つく.

contrast_examples.jp: 部下に示しがつかない。
contrast_examples.en: It wouldn't set a good example for subordinates.

prompt.context_jp: 「今の話 くれぐれも___で！」
prompt.prompt_jp: くれぐれも___で！
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the fixed phrase meaning 'keep this strictly confidential.'

feedback.correct_en: 他言無用 (たごんむよう) = 'no telling others / strictly confidential' — a stock phrase for gossip Shibazaki is sharing.
feedback.incorrect_en: 他人無用 and 他事無用 are not standard idioms.

prompt.context_jp: 「___を返すようですが…」
prompt.prompt_jp: ___を返すようですが…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the noun in this polite 'with respect, but...' preface.

feedback.correct_en: お言葉を返すようですが is the set polite phrase used before respectfully contradicting a superior — exactly Mai's situation.
feedback.incorrect_en: お話 and ご返事 don't form this idiomatic 'with respect, but...' preface.

contrast_examples.jp: お言葉を返すようですが、私は反対です。

contrast_examples.en: I'll hear what you have to say.

prompt.context_jp: 「あいつ ___が入ると もう 周りが見えなくなるとこあって」
prompt.prompt_jp: あいつ___が入るともう周りが見えなくなる
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the noun describing Mai 'getting fired up.'

feedback.correct_en: スイッチが入る is the natural idiom for 'to flip into intense mode / get fired up' about a person.
feedback.incorrect_en: エンジンがかかる exists (warming up) but doesn't collocate with 入る. ギアが入る is used for shifting gears but not for a person's emotional switch.

contrast_examples.jp: 仕事のスイッチが入る。
やっとエンジンがかかってきた。

prompt.context_jp: 相馬が舞に、新田に抗議しても無駄だと言う場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural for Souma dismissing Mai's plan?

choices.text: あの人に何言ったって 響きやしない
あの人に何を言っても 響くことはしない
あの人に何かを言うと 響かないよ

feedback.correct_en: 〜たって+〜やしない is the natural blunt/colloquial pattern for 'no matter what you say, it won't get through'. This is the actual line in the story.
feedback.incorrect_en: 響くことはしない is unnatural (響く is intransitive). 何かを言うと shifts the meaning to a specific conditional, losing the 'no matter what' nuance.

contrast_examples.jp: 何を言ったって無駄だ。
contrast_examples.en: No matter what you say, it's useless.
If I say something, I get scolded. (different meaning)

prompt.context_jp: Mai explains why she remembers the customers.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing is most natural for Mai's remark?

choices.text: お客さまのこと覚えるのは テラーの基本ですから
お客さまを覚えるのは テラーの基礎ですから
お客さまのことは テラーが覚える基本ですから

feedback.correct_en: 〜のことを覚える is the idiomatic way to say 'remember a person'; テラーの基本 is a natural collocation ('a teller's basic duty').
feedback.incorrect_en: お客さまを覚える drops ことof the standard idiom; 基礎 means foundational knowledge, not a job basic. Option c is tangled syntactically.

contrast_examples.en: To learn the basics of the job.

prompt.context_jp: Mai's climactic rejection of the banking motto.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version delivers Mai's blunt, emphatic rebuke most naturally?

choices.text: そんな常識なんて… クソ食らえ！
そのような常識は… クソ食らえ！
そんな常識は… クソを食べてください！

feedback.correct_en: 〜なんて+クソ食らえ captures the dismissive, emotional punch Mai delivers. なんて adds 'the likes of such a thing', fitting her outrage.
feedback.incorrect_en: そのような is too formal for this outburst. 'クソを食べてください' literalizes the idiom politely, which is absurd and unnatural.

contrast_examples.jp: そんなルールなんてクソ食らえ！
contrast_examples.en: To hell with rules like that!

contrast_examples.jp: そのような規則は不適切です。

prompt.context_jp: Mai frustrated with Souma's resignation.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version best captures Mai's exasperated question?

choices.text: どうして そんなに簡単に 諦めちゃうんですか？
なぜ そんなに簡単に 諦めてしまいますか？
どうして そんなに簡単に 諦めることですか？

feedback.correct_en: 諦めちゃう (contracted 諦めてしまう) + んですか gives the natural emotional/exasperated tone Mai uses with her boss.
feedback.incorrect_en: 諦めてしまいますか is grammatically off (〜てしまう normally doesn't form this question form). Option c garbles the structure.

contrast_examples.jp: どうして泣いちゃうの？
contrast_examples.en: Why do you end up crying?

prompt.context_jp: Mai proposing a counterattack to Souma.
prompt.prompt_en: Which proposal sounds most natural in context?

choices.text: 相馬さん リベンジしませんか？
相馬さん リベンジをいたしましょうか？
相馬さん リベンジすることにしますか？

feedback.correct_en: 〜しませんか is the standard polite-but-friendly invitation form, matching Mai's energetic suggestion to her boss.
feedback.incorrect_en: いたしましょうか is too humble/formal for this moment. 〜することにしますか sounds like asking whether to decide, not inviting.

contrast_examples.jp: ご一緒いたしましょうか？
